To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — So this happened. Fernhollow Photo is officially a thing!!

I have news!! Big news, not another dog. Pickle is still an only child and still has unresolved issues with the lamp.

Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business. My business. I’m going out on my own as a wedding photographer, and typing that where my entire family can read it is somehow scarier than filing the actual paperwork.

I wanted to tell you all before Thanksgiving because I would like to get through at least one helping of stuffing without trying to explain an LLC across Aunt Ruthie’s table. Also because I’m really, really excited, and you should know that part first.

The short version: Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October. Marisol told me on October 6, and after four years shooting for her, it was a lot to take in. I’m going to miss it. Four years is a lot of weddings, a lot of sore feet, a lot of figuring out how to get the picture when the schedule has gone completely sideways and somebody cannot find the groom’s brother.

Marisol basically taught me everything. I came out of those four years a much better photographer, and a lot of that is because she trusted me with things before I quite trusted myself. She also told me I was ready for this. Apparently she’s thought so for about two years, which would have been useful information for my brain to accept a little earlier.

Six of the weddings on my calendar for next year came through her referrals. That is an enormous vote of confidence. Marisol, if you’re reading this, thank you. For those couples, for the last four years, for all of it. I don’t know how to make this paragraph less mushy so we’re just going to leave it.

This is a big change, but it isn’t an idea I came up with three weeks ago while unsupervised on the internet. I’ve been planning some version of it in my head for two years. The studio closing meant it was time to stop thinking “eventually” and actually do the paperwork.

Which I did on October 22, on my lunch break, sitting in the car outside a Fred Meyer.

Very glamorous. Exactly how you picture starting your own photography business. Filed the LLC, cried a little. There was no ribbon cutting, just me in a parking lot having a fairly major life moment next to people who were trying to buy groceries.

The website went live November 1. Fernhollow Photo LLC exists. There are forms and everything.

And before anybody starts composing a concerned comment, here is the part with actual planning in it.

I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. FOURTEEN. Six are Marisol referrals, and eight found me on my own. That’s not a wish list or fourteen people who said “we should totally talk.” They are booked weddings on my calendar. June is already the busiest month, with four, and I’ll be heading all the way out to Wallowa Lake in September.

Jae will second shoot the big weddings with me, paid per wedding. So I’ll have another photographer there when I need one, rather than attempting to be in two places at once. I have tried that. Still only one of me, unfortunately for the wedding timeline and fortunately for everyone who has to listen to me talk about lenses.

And Dad: HEALTH INSURANCE IS SORTED.

I picked a marketplace plan. It starts January 1. I love you. I know why you ask. You can still ask me how work is going, but please let this paragraph count as the health insurance portion of Thanksgiving.

I’m not pretending that fourteen bookings means every part of running a business will be easy. I know taking the pictures and running the whole thing are not exactly the same job. There’s plenty to learn, and yes, I’m scared. But I have a plan, I have work booked, and I’ve spent four years doing the work itself. I want to give this a real shot.

The booking that made it feel real in a completely different way was Dahlia and Ken. June 12, Timberline. They found me because of the pictures I took of one of Marisol’s couples at Multnomah Falls, and they wanted me to photograph their wedding.

That was my first booking that felt 100% mine. They saw my pictures, liked them, and picked me. I know that is technically how hiring a photographer works. Still. When it happens with your own name on everything, it does something weird to your chest.

I’m going to photograph their wedding at Timberline next June. Sorry, needed to say it again.

Also, the name! Grandma, this part is for you.

Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. Long before I knew what I was doing, and definitely before I knew this could be my job.

When I was trying to name the business, I kept coming back to that place. I wanted a name I could live with for a long time, and that one already meant something to me. It feels right that the thing I’m starting now is named for somewhere I started with you.

So yes, Grandma, the name is for you. Now everybody knows and you’re allowed to tell people.

Sam made a cake to celebrate. It said FERNHOLOW.

One L missing. Extremely supportive cake, questionable proofreading. We ate it anyway. I don’t think the LLC people need to hear about the cake discrepancy.

I keep going back and forth between being ridiculously excited and remembering some small business thing I need to figure out. Then I look at next year’s calendar again. There are actual couples on there who want me at their weddings, and I cannot wait to get to work.

Anyway. That’s my big news. Your regularly scheduled pictures of Pickle will return, probably very soon, because he remains available for portraits and has no respect for my office hours.

Mom, yes, Sam is coming to Thanksgiving. We’re bringing rolls and the cranberry thing.

And does anybody want free family pictures while we’re all at Ruthie’s? I’ll bring the camera. We can step outside before dinner if people are up for it. No pressure, but if you’ve been meaning to get a picture with your kids or your person or Grandma, grab me. Uncle Greg, we can try to get yours done before you freeze this time.

Love you all. I’m nervous and happy and very ready to tell you about this without a turkey between us.

Fernhollow Photo!! That’s me!!
